gaps.text: Still the 36-line stub: 8 grey boxes, tan plane, NO ceiling at all. Biggest gap in the project.

Content gap, not a rendering gap. (1) Product facings are flat colour fields with grey bars instead of real printed type — ~60% of the tell. (2) ~8 box meshes recoloured, 5-8 identical copies per shelf; real shelves carry 6-15 SKUs of mixed height/width and something on nearly every shelf is a bottle/jar/pouch/bag. (3) Zero 'shopped' disorder — every face perfectly flush, unrotated, evenly spaced, no sold-out voids.

Contact shadows / AO is now the single biggest tell — products have no darkening where they meet the deck, shelf cavities do not fall off to near-black, so shelves read as decals floating on a plane. Then: no per-instance variation WITHIN a facing block (20 identical chip bags, same lean, zero gaps); shelves 100% full when real stores run 10-20% gaps; everything the same matte diffuse with zero specular events.

The two surfaces filling the largest solid angle of the frame — ceiling and floor — are still flat-shaded planes with a texture on them. (1) The floor returns ZERO specular under a lit ceiling; every real photo shows the ceiling light rows mirrored as long vertical smears. 'Until light physically bounces off the floor, nothing further up the list will matter.' (2) Ceiling troffers are emissive quads coplanar with the tile, not recessed housings with tube shapes and a shadow line. (3) BINARY TELLS: an unlit pink placeholder cube on a grey stick, untextured grey cart proxies, a blank grey plane where a sign texture failed. Any one ends the test alone.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS OF THE LOOP, NOT THE STORE: 'You fixed the three tells the last critic named. You did not fix the CLASS of problem those tells belonged to. This is the sixth round of that pattern - a critic names a symptom, the symptom gets repaired precisely, and the next critic picks a different symptom from the identical underlying class and calls it just as fast.' The class is LIGHT TRANSPORT and CONTENT ENTROPY. On the glass: 'You added the OPACITY of a reflection without adding the IMAGE. That is the same mistake as the r4 painted-decal floor, one surface over.' #1 fix, and it says if you do exactly one thing do this: contact shadows and AO at every junction - 'nothing in these frames is in contact with anything.'

THE CEILING gave up all four frames in two seconds, before a floor, a shelf base or a pane of glass was looked at: troffers show ZERO falloff with distance (the far one is as bright as the near one), they are single flat white rectangles where real ones show 2-4 discrete tubes with dark gaps and neighbouring fixtures at different colour temperatures, and the sprinkler main has no heads, no couplings and casts no shadow on the deck 150mm below it. Second: occlusion COVERAGE, not calibration - the refrigerated case run, the largest single occluder in the set, measures 31-58.5%, at or worse than last round's baseline, and several plain gondola bases have no measurable skirt at all. Third: the kick plate is an 18-19px band of near-constant black with a hard step, where real is a LIT kick darkening over 6px - occlusion is mutual and continuous across a junction, a smooth V, not a black slab followed by a ramp.

HANDOFF FROM builder-cctv-r8, measured independently and NOT reachable from the grade: THE CEILING TROFFERS ARE NOT LIGHT SOURCES. Reference photographs blow 0.56-3.1% of their pixels (median 0.98%); the game's floor view blows 0.028%. cctv proved it cannot be fixed on its side - pushing grade 'highlight' 0.33 -> 0.55 buys only 0.31% and then stops responding (0.75 is WORSE than 0.55; the shoulder is saturated). It is an emissive level in store.js. Note this is the same axis as builder-store-r11's own largest open item: ceiling/floor luminance ratio 1.341 against references at 0.857/0.959/0.380.

SHELF-FACE CHROMA NEVER REACHES A SATURATED BLOCK. The store's own albedo is loud - per-instance colours on the 70 run meshes measure CIELAB C* mean 41.0 across 38,008 facings, 46.0% of them above C*45 - but the framebuffer is not. On three clean plates the median block (5% of box width) measures C* 13.9/15.0/14.9 and only 0.3%/1.3%/4.0% of blocks exceed C*34; the six grocery-aisle references run median 21.1-30.0 with 4.0-45.3% of blocks over C*34 (median 26.3%). Conditioned on lightness so exposure cannot be the explanation, render shelf pixels at L*35-50 sit at C* 13.1-17.7 against photographs at 13.8-45.5 (median 29.9), and render chroma is FLAT across every L* bin (13-15 everywhere) where photographs peak at L*35-50 and fall off. On the builder's own round-5 hue instrument the render carries 0.0-5.2% of shelf pixels in the blue band at sat>0.32 against 13.3-23.5% in the two Langenstein's photographs it was calibrated on, and 13.7-30.3% saturated overall against 30.9-81.8%. The render's dry-grocery aisles score like reference/store_04's all-white frozen reach-in, the least colourful photograph in the set. Not the specular veil: zeroing specular on all 70 run materials moves C* only 15.85->16.20 (+2.2%, restore verified byte-identical). A neutral dim from albedo L*61.5 to the rendered L*41.8 predicts C*30.6 - the reference median - so roughly half the chroma is lost in the product shading path beyond exposure. Evidence: shots/critic_r11_chroma_ab.png

That is the thing to find. The render's dry-grocery aisles currently score like store_04's all-white frozen reach-in, the least colourful photograph in the set. High-chroma outliers in the render are all POP signage, never product.

Shelf faces are lit ~1 stop under: product pixels sit 12.3 L* BELOW their own frame median (photos: +1.4, range -11 to +5), so 1.3% of product reaches L*>65 where photographs put 20-47%. The chroma that survives into L*50-65 is the achromatic bare-stock texel: C* 7.4 vs 22.7 in five named photo shelf regions (0.32x) while L*20-35 and 35-50 are already at 0.91x and 0.85x. Live ablation, byte-identical restore: scaling the four store lights x2.0 moves product medL* 39.4->52.5 and the L*50-65 bin 7.4->19.7 with ZERO texture change. Round 12 fixed the albedo; the lighting is eating it.

THE SHELF FACES ARE LIT ABOUT A STOP UNDER. It is not colour any more - round 12 fixed the albedo and the LIGHTING is eating it. Render product at stage-4 albedo has a healthy photographic distribution: median L* 65.2, 33.1% of pixels in L* 65-80, 17.2% above 80. At the framebuffer: median L* 39.4, 1.3% above L* 65, 0.1% above L* 80. Five named photo shelf regions: median L* 41.9-61.7, 20-47% above L* 65, 4-28% above L* 80. Stated exposure-invariantly so no grade can game it: RENDER PRODUCT SITS 12.3 L* BELOW ITS OWN FRAME MEDIAN; the same regions in photographs sit +1.4 (range -11 to +5). This is also what makes the remaining chroma hole - per-pixel median C* by L* bin, render vs photo: 20-35 0.91x, 35-50 0.85x, 50-65 0.32x, 65-80 0.68x. Every bin is fine except L* 50-65, and the survivors into it are the near-white bare-stock texels. LIVE ABLATION, byte-identical restore, one page load: scaling the four store lights x2.0 moves product medL* 39.4->52.5, %L*>65 1.3->23.7, and the L* 50-65 chroma bin 7.4->19.7 against the photo's 22.7 - WITH NO TEXTURE CHANGE AT ALL. Global x2 is NOT the fix: it lifts floor and ceiling too, and whole-frame medL* is already correct at 51.7 against a 49 reference median. The fix is light REACHING THE GONDOLA FACE.

Product wall has no bright end. Lit product pixels above L*65: render 4.25% (6 poses, exact stage-7 mask, range 1.1-8.4) vs references 22.6-26.2% (14 files, median stable across 4 selectors, min 10.6). Above L*80: 0.32% vs 6.5-8.1%. Round 12->13 moved it 1.52->4.25 — real, about one fifth of the way. This is what I keyed on in every blind product tile.

CORRECTED (supersedes my earlier r13 gap line, which overstated it by comparing the render's product MASK against whole photographs — there is no product mask for a photograph). On ONE RULE APPLIED TO BOTH SIDES, pixels with C*>20, whole frame, no mask, no rectangle: the BODY of the render's chromatic population sits ~7 L* dark. median L* 43.2 [40.3-44.4] vs photo 50.1 [40.6-63.1]; p75 55.4 vs 62.6; and only 21.3% of the frame is chromatic [12.0-26.1] vs photo 32.8 [18.4-72.8], near the bottom of the range. THE BLIND TEST DOES NOT TURN ON THE STATISTIC THIS ROUND OPTIMISED. My own blind A/B - fresh tiles, my six poses, key md5 a758c6a0 written before I looked, one rule both sides (identical normalised crop forced to a common aspect so aspect is never the cue, LANCZOS downscale in linear light, then PIL q87 4:2:0 on BOTH sides) - scored 36/36 with 18/18 render recall, and 34/36 on my cold calls before I used the 6/6 balance constraint. Every call came from three cues and not one of them is chromatic lightness: (1) generated package and promo copy, legible and category-incoherent - PENNYWHISTLE MARINARA SAUCE / KETTLE COOKED FOR EXTRA CRUNCH, WINDROW CHOCOLATE CHIPS / MARGINALLY GLUTEN FREE, and NEW LOW / CLUB DEAL / MANAGER SPECIAL straight out of the HEADS grammar; (2) the two shelf runs are bilaterally symmetric in colour blocking and pitch, which no real aisle is; (3) at aisle distance the floor is one continuous mottle with no tile joints, where store_03 / store_07 / store_12 all resolve grout. The L* body gap is real and I show below it is cheap to close, but closing it will not move this test. Round 15 should price those three.

THE CUE, AND IT IS NOT LIGHTING: generated package copy that is legible and CATEGORY-INCOHERENT (PENNYWHISTLE MARINARA SAUCE / KETTLE COOKED FOR EXTRA CRUNCH); bilateral symmetry of the two shelf runs; and the distant floor reading as one continuous mottle where store_03 / store_07 / store_12 resolve grout. The L* body gap is real and I show it is cheap to close, but closing it moves nothing on the actual bar.

THE COPY FIX CHANGED THE SIZE OF THE POOL, NOT THE FACT THAT IT IS ONE. 36 of 44 classes hold more than one distinct product and 132 of 140 SKUs share all six copy bands with a different product, so the department-level incoherence became class-level incoherence. Over 200,000 sampled copyFor() draws under 40 declared rules, 27.4% of facings carry at least one contradiction and all 40 rules are reachable: RAPID RELEASE / COUGH SYRUP / PAIN RELIEVER-FEVER REDUCER / 100 COUNT; ZERO SUGAR / DIET COLA / 110 CALORIES; VOLUMIZING / BAR SOAP / 15 FL OZ; PRE-SIFTED / PURE CANE SUGAR / 100% WHOLE GRAIN; CRUNCHY / GRAPE JELLY / 12g PROTEIN; SEEDED / HAMBURGER BUNS / 20 SLICES PER LOAF; JALAPENO / CARAMEL POPCORN / KETTLE COOKED FOR EXTRA CRUNCH. copyCheck() returns [] and cannot see any of them - it asks whether a SKU has a class, never whether a band fits the SKU. AND THE SAME BUG IS UNTOUCHED IN THE SIGNS: promoDeal(seed) and promoCard(g,W,H,seed) take no department, so SAVE $12.89 PER LB prints over SNACKS/CHIPS and FROZEN ONLY prints over PAPER/CLEANING - I called both blind before reading any source. But the deeper gap is that NO STATISTIC REPRODUCES THE CALL: flat-field fraction gets 24/36 and colour richness 25/36 against my eye 36/36. The cue is semantic. The render contains no depicted real-world object - every package is type on flat colour plus one repeated plated-food oval, every sign is the store own template grammar. A human recognises nothing on any facing and calls it. Round 16 should stop hunting a statistic and put real depicted subjects on the packages.

Siblings on the same sheet: THISTLEDOWN TOOTHPASTE carrying a shampoo ingredient list (guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride, betaine, glycerin) and RECYCLE THE BOTTLE on a carton, because legal=care is shared between bodycare and oral.

r16 INSTRUMENT CAVEAT for the next round, and it is NOT the one the brief names. snapClean(storeOnly) is byte-identical on 2 of my 3 poses across two captures in one page load, but F1_face_a3 differs on 5,561 px (0.60% of frame) at a max channel delta of 16/255. The differing pixels are NOT the back-wall freezer glass — the bbox is (347,427)-(695,615), which is the REFLECTIVE FLOOR in the mid-ground beside the endcap. So there are at least two sources of clean-plate wobble on this piece, and a paired comparison at a pose that includes mid-ground floor needs a tolerance rather than a hash compare. I did not touch floor.js this round; r15 uSeamAlb is uncommitted in the tree and is the likely owner.

THE ATLAS IS A 48-CELL PIPE AND THE ROUND WROTE 82 MOTIFS INTO IT. ATLAS in pack.js is carton 6x4, pouch 4x2, can 4x2, bottle 4x2 = 48 cells, fixed, baked once. CELL_LOG confirms 48. So the whole store holds 30 of the 81 assigned motifs, 40 of 140 product nouns and 30 of 58 brand names, and 51 motifs are never drawn anywhere - including three of the four the round leads with: peachHalf, spaghetti and toothpaste are all in the never-drawn list. Only babyFace of the four is baked. 44853 package instances draw from those 48 artworks. Brand colour IS per-instance and nearly unique (2485 distinct colours over 4194 carton instances in run0.0), so the correct statement is not that 48 pictures repeat - it is that colour varies continuously while every glyph, every layout and every motif is one of 48, which is precisely why the eye reads instancing. depictCheck() asserts every SKU has a motif and every motif has a SKU; it never asks whether the SKU is ever baked, so it passes at 100% while 63% of the work does not ship. Same shape at the other surface: 370 danglers and 93 promo headers draw from 16 cards each, and of the 8 department-gated qualifiers exactly ONE appears in the shipped store (promo cell 9, health, ADULT USE ONLY) - FROZEN ONLY and PLUS DEPOSIT are 0 of 32 cards, so 17.07% and 11.39% describe the grammar, not the build. Widening the carton atlas is one texture and it is the only change that can put the round-16 work in front of a player.

ROUND PACKAGES DESTROY THEIR OWN ARTWORK, AND THAT IS NOW THE CUE. 23.0% of all 44,853 package instances (10,333: can/bottle lathes + cylinders) wrap the atlas cell around a body of revolution, and the print degenerates into vertical smear. Gradient anisotropy mean|dL/dx| / mean|dL/dy|, masks taken by ABLATION so no region is declared: round-form facings 1.490 +/- 0.372 sd relative to flat-form facings in the SAME frame at the SAME distance, 6/6 poses above 1.0, range 1.075-2.062, all six restores byte-identical. Three reference photographs run through the identical rule put REAL cylinders BELOW their flat neighbours: 0.730 (store_01 tuna cans vs pouches), 0.783 (store_00_Drinks bottles vs cartons), 1.033 (store_05 Lipton bottles vs paper packs). The sign is inverted. In the round-only ablation not one cylinder in the store carries a readable wordmark, a rim ellipse or a lid, while CEDAR MILL ROASTED PEANUTS reads as a frosted bottle with a barcode across its face. REFUTATION PUBLISHED: whole-frame anisotropy does NOT separate — render 0.654-0.776 median 0.706 sits inside references 0.617-1.164 median 0.874, n=14 of 14 files. The separation is the within-frame class contrast, not the frame. The flat-faced work is genuinely good and is no longer what I called on: OAKHAVEN MILK CHOCOLATE BARS, HAVENWOOD PEPPERONI PIZZA with NUTRITION FACTS and NET WT 10 OZ (283g), MARCHETTI INSTANT OATMEAL with a legible steaming bowl. Round 15 said the cue is semantic; it is not any more. It is material.

A REAL CAN IS BANDED HORIZONTALLY by its label, rim and lid, so its anisotropy sits BELOW a carton; the render sits above. NOT ONE CYLINDER IN THE STORE CARRIES A READABLE WORDMARK, A RIM ELLIPSE OR A LID - CEDAR MILL ROASTED PEANUTS reads as a frosted bottle with a barcode printed across its face, and one lathe in the canned aisle reads as a GREEN WINE GOBLET, a silhouette that belongs in no grocery aisle. TWO REFUTATIONS AGAINST MY OWN HEADLINE: my first instrument said round facings carry MORE gradient energy, not less, so less ink is FALSE and the defect is DIRECTIONAL not quantitative; and whole-frame anisotropy does not separate at all, render 0.654-0.776 median 0.706 sitting INSIDE references 0.617-1.164 median 0.874 over 14 of 14 files. The separation lives in the within-frame class contrast, not the frame.
Sign inverted but magnitude short: render K 0.894 against photographs 0.612, i.e. +46%. A real can wall is banded harder than this one.

Every hanging sign and promo tag comes from ONE design system: numbered blade + two-word category list + three or four lozenge layouts, all flat matte vector, no vendor identity, no photographic content. 13 of my 14 blind render calls came off that grammar and the mirrored-corridor geometry; ZERO came off a package, which is the round real achievement. store_00_Drinks carries five colliding systems in one frame — a backlit strawberry lightbox with icon chips, per-slat wooden category markers, separate black category hangers, a Campbell-branded sale POS, a Keurig endcap. r15 concluded the render contains no depicted real-world object; r18 closed that on the facings and it is still true of every sign in the store.

AND ALL THREE NEW ASSERTIONS CERTIFY CLEAN UNDER INJECTION: latheCheck() returns [] with all 51 lathes carrying r17 index-based v LIVE ON THE GPU at worst stretch 6.0x and barrel v-span 0.099, because it reads LATHE_LOG written once at BAKE TIME and never the geometry - so the round own uvAB() corrupts the store while the check certifies it, which is the brief own guards-an-earlier-stage failure one round after it was written down. aspectCheck() passes 11/11 outlines while 38 SHIPPED INSTANCES REACH 4.22:1, past the widest declared band of 3.80, because the aspect comes from a per-instance non-uniform scale (3.2-3.6x more in y than x) that a check reading only the K table cannot see - the r17 goblet reached a shelf through exactly a downstream path. And typeCheck() self-test reproduces exactly, but setTypeCtx is called for only four atlases, so THE ENTIRE SHELF-TAG ATLAS SITS OUTSIDE THE GUARANTEE: 10 raw fillText sites including the price numerals at CH*0.46, plus a fitText(CLEARANCE) whose contrast step silently no-ops. It contributes 0 of 688 logged runs - ON THE PRICE RAIL, which the brief lists as bar item #4.

The aisle volume is empty. This is a SEMANTIC cue, about what objects exist and where they are, not a colour or brightness statistic - I could not make any of three photometric proxies separate the classes. In every reference photograph the space between the two shelf faces is continuously invaded by paper and wire: clip strips of impulse product hung on a hook into the aisle, wobblers on plastic arms sticking out perpendicular, coupon dispensers, wire dividers and peg hooks, cables, hand-taped signs at odd angles, and product overhanging the lip. In reference/store_03_Food_aisle_at_Publix crop (1300,560)-(1900,898) I count four such objects in one 600px crop; in reference/store_02_Langensteins_grocery crop (1180,380)-(1720,684) three. In all twelve r20 plates the count is zero to two, and every one of those is the same thing: a flat, camera-facing, zero-thickness billboard quad with no shadow and no overlap onto the product behind it - GET 1 FREE in near_a4 at roughly x 960-1280 y 240-420, PRICE DROP in near_a7, MARKDOWN 33c in chase_a1. There is not one hook, one wire, one dangler, one curled taped sign, or one item pushed forward past its neighbours anywhere in the set. The consequence is that the shelf-edge line reads as an unbroken ruler-straight bar from gondola end to gondola end, and that silhouette is what I called on first in all six poses, including the three chase poses where no product text is legible at all. Fix is geometry, not shading: put a few hundred small objects into the volume between the shelf lip and the aisle centre, at arbitrary angles, with thickness and contact shadows.

The shelf cavity is not a cavity. A gondola shelf is a three-sided box and light has to get into it, so in the reference photographs the underside of a shelf, the back panel and the deck under a product sit at 0.19 to 0.42 of the brightness of that same shelf's own lit lip - tile_45 from store_03_Food_aisle_at_Pub#0 x380-520 lip y118-126 = 112.3 versus cavity y165-205 = 22.0, ratio 0.20, and tile_43 from store_01_Langenstein_s_Sup#2 x120-200 lip y196-203 = 174.9 versus cavity y237-254 = 74.0, ratio 0.42 still falling to 0.24 by y273. The render sits at 0.59 to 0.87 - tile_19 x40-120 lip y202-209 = 173.8 versus cavity y225-242 = 150.5, ratio 0.87, and tile_47 x380-500 lip y186-193 = 186.3 versus cavity y201-220 = 120.8, ratio 0.65. The occlusion dynamic range is compressed about 3x, identically in control and after, so no surface ever reads as being inside a box and no object reads as resting on the deck it stands on. This is SEMANTIC, not photometric: it is about WHERE light is missing relative to geometry, not how much light there is on average - which is exactly why all five brightness and colour statistics failed. Do not chase a global number. Occlude the ambient term.

Product faces are flat-shaded proxies, not printed packaging. SEMANTIC, not photometric. Every render facing is a single flat colour field wearing a wordmark or a vector glyph; every photograph facing is full-bleed print with internal structure - brand mark, illustration, colour bands, legal panel - and differs from the facing beside it. Named instance: near_a4_700_240 region 190,115-400,210, repeated facings of one crimson case each carrying a grey vector bottle outline, against store_01 Langenstein region 0,20-210,115. Second instance: near_a7_880_400 region 222,120-330,185, every carton face one flat grey field with a dark rectangle standing in for a label. This is what I called every one of the 18 renders on, in under a second each, and it survives the 45x32 downsample with every glyph destroyed - renders read as large flat single-hue slabs, photographs as a fine mosaic. No brightness or colour statistic will close it; it needs real printed pack art and more distinct SKUs per run of shelf.

Product facings have no third dimension. Every rank-and-file facing is a single flat co-planar billboard - no top face, no side face, no thickness - separated by constant-width pure-black voids. This is SEMANTIC: it is missing geometry, not a colour or brightness statistic. Round 22 painted a gold side panel onto the billboard, and a painted side panel is geometrically impossible: measured on 11 named instances in row y=604-676 of the near_a4 frame, with every band inspected before it was counted, band width is mean 4.09 px sd 1.78, and the correlation between band width and distance from the optical axis at x=640 is NEGATIVE at -0.24 - the widest bands (6, 7, 6, 6 px) sit near the axis at offsets +66 to +212 while the narrowest (3, 2, 4 px) sit at the frame edge at +398, +442, +494. A real box side face must do the opposite: widen toward the frame edge and flip from the left of a facing to the right as it crosses the axis. Here the band is on the same side of every facing at every position, because it is texture. Compare panel C: three adjacent HOLLIS facings at (168,352)-(350,460) against three adjacent Capn Crunch boxes in store_00_Drinks at (1430,835)-(1710,1000) - the real cartons show top faces, side faces, varied depth and angle, and print wrapping the corner; the render shows three identical flat planes and black slots. This is why four spot inks bought nothing: the round improved the artwork printed on the billboard while the tell is that it is a billboard.

Every package shares one global orientation. No unit is individually yawed, so within a rank all carton vertical edges are mutually parallel and lean the same way, side-face width is constant, adjacent units are separated by constant-width dark slots instead of touching, and top edges are collinear. Real cartons each sit at their own small random yaw, so side-face width varies unit to unit at the SAME offset, boxes touch, and top edges splay. Named instances, all q88 4:2:0 from one encoder: render tile_16 (430,600)-(720,715) near-vertical edge-angle IQR 7.38 deg and tile_02 (430,600)-(720,715) IQR 7.13, against photograph tile_11 (0,255)-(330,420) IQR 17.50. A second identical q88 round-trip moves the render numbers to 9.10 and 9.06 and the photo to 16.98, so the codec shrinks the gap rather than creating it. CAUTION: sd of the same instrument does NOT separate - 8.74 and 7.66 render against 8.71 for photo tile_18 - only IQR does, so this is offered as corroboration of a hand-checked structural observation on named instances, not as a population statistic. This cue is SEMANTIC, a fact about how product is placed, not photometric - photometrically the render is fine and flatness and edge width are correctly retired.

ONE BRDF FOR THE WHOLE STORE - every material answers the light identically. PHOTOMETRIC, not semantic. Named instances, coordinates in the 720x720 tile frame, all three boxes verified by magnifying them: RENDER bay shots/blind_qv0ue76q/tile_14.jpg (150,90)-(390,330) holds a rigid plastic jar at (166,140)-(200,180), a flexible film pouch at (296,150)-(336,182) and the shelf lip at (250,196)-(290,216). Their luminance p99.5 is 0.84, 0.68, 0.66. The film pouch, which is the glossiest thing on any real supermarket shelf, is DARKER than the rigid jar beside it and neither approaches white; the metal lip is the darkest of the three. Material has no effect on how bright a surface is allowed to get. PHOTOGRAPH bay shots/blind_gq43ambk/tile_09.jpg (240,20)-(480,260) holds a printed carton at (250,170)-(290,202), film wrap at (300,50)-(340,82) and the shelf lip at (296,116)-(336,136), reading 0.85, 1.00, 0.99: the film and the lip both clip to white while the carton stays mid, and that spread IS the material. This is why the scale ladder looks the way it does. A single face gives no reference - you cannot tell matte from glossy without something in frame that is glossy - so at 46px I score 14/20. A shelf bay puts film, carton, glass, plastic and metal under one light in one crop, and in the render all five come back as the same matte substance with different colours painted on. That is a bay-scale photometric cue and it is not on the retired list: it is not facing flatness, not edge transition width, not repetition, not a cavity or lip or trough statistic, and not any image-row profile on a receding surface. Give the store more than one BRDF - a specular lobe on film, foil and moulded plastic, and a sharper one on the shelf lip and the jar - before touching package orientation again.

One BRDF for the whole store - but the mechanism is wrong: four distinct per-family Phong specs have existed since round 2 and the round-13 note in that same file says the specular has never once put a highlight on a product facing. It is a DELIVERY failure, not an authoring one.

Shelf-edge signage is floating decals, not physical card. SEMANTIC, not photometric. At tile_11 (350,290)-(560,470), identical in both arms, a green package hovers unsupported and tilted in mid-air and clips straight through the red SALE banner; the SALE card and the RECIPE pad above it are dead-flat planes with zero edge thickness. At tile_02 (430,150)-(540,270) the NEW 4.27 dangler's hanger wire terminates in empty space attached to nothing and the card passes in front of the price label with a hard aliased zero-thickness edge. Every photograph shelf-talker is the opposite - see tile_18 (60,40)-(190,120): thick card stock, visibly bent, clipped into a holder, hanging with gravity skew, casting a soft shadow. This is present in all 9 render tiles, is untouched by r25, and survives every codec control because it is geometry rather than tone. It also explains the scale ladder: unresolvable at 46 px, obvious from 240 px up. CONFIDENCE: the observation is high - reproducible at the published coordinates in both arms. The mechanism is only a hypothesis - promo cards look like camera-facing textured quads placed without a collision test against product geometry. It is falsified if any card anywhere shows a lit side face, which would make them thin geometry rather than decals, or if the green package turns out to be parented to a peg hidden behind the banner.

Shelf-edge signage is floating decals, not physical card - a package hovers unsupported and clips through a SALE banner, cards are dead-flat planes with zero edge thickness, a dangler's hanger wire terminates in empty space. Observation high confidence, mechanism a hypothesis, falsifiers named.

BIGGEST REMAINING CUE - the price rail has no cross-section and the price tags are decals painted on it. OBSERVATION, confidence HIGH: in shots/blind_8pqtljj5/tile_09.jpg the bare shelf edge at crop (330,495)-(470,545) is ONE flat plane - deck gradient down to a hard black boundary, with no upper return, no lower return, no channel, no groove and no shadow line anywhere across it. The tags on it are unclipped rectangles at inconsistent heights: the 2.39 SUNCREST instance spans y=514..533 while the rail face ends at y=529, so the tag hangs 4 px BELOW its own holder, and its neighbour 13 px to the left starts 5 px higher with nothing registering either to a datum. No tag has a side face, casts a shadow on the rail, or leaves a gap behind it. The matched photograph at shots/blind_8pqtljj5/tile_05.jpg crop (150,206)-(330,274) shows the same object as a folded channel with four separately lit facets - deck roll, bright upper return, RECESSED tag trough, lower return with a dark underside - and its tags sit behind the upper return, which shadows their top edge. This is the exact disease round 26 named, on the population round 26 said it did not fix, and it is the most repeated object class in the frame: 20 to 35 instances per render tile, on every lip, in every bay, in all 18 render tiles of both arms. EXPLANATION, confidence MEDIUM and this is the half four critics running have got wrong: the rail is a box or a single quad with no return flanges, and each price tag is a separate quad at railFront plus epsilon sized from its artwork rather than from a channel opening, so there is nothing to clip it and nothing to shadow it. FALSIFIER 1 - if the returns already exist in geometry, a normals pass on any near pose shows 3 or more distinct normals across the lip; I predict 1 or 2, and if it shows 3 or more my mechanism is wrong and the cue is shading, not geometry. FALSIFIER 2 - if tags are already sized to the channel, no tag bounding box exceeds the rail front-face height; I predict many do, starting with the two named above. FALSIFIER 3, THE ONE THAT MATTERS - build the returns, clip the tags, re-render the same three near poses and run the forced choice. If it comes back at chance the mechanism was right and the percept still is not there, which is what has happened four rounds running. A measured change with no percept is not a closed cue. ---- LEAK 8, AND IT IS OPEN RIGHT NOW: the harness's own leak-5 guard REJECTS both of this round's sets. Running r24_blindset.render_tiles('r26on') on the shipped plates raises SystemExit - arm r26on contributed near_a1, near_a4, near_a7, needs a NEAR and a CHASE pose, or the render side is all flat-on shelf face against corridor-view photographs. It can never pass: the best CHASE window in the building is prod 0.257 (chase_a6, both arms) and MIN_PROD_R24 is 0.30, so raising the threshold to close leak 5's density half made leak 5's framing half unsatisfiable and the two halves cancel. These sets cannot be regenerated by the code on disk. SECOND HALF - prod_frac is called ONLY inside render_tiles; photo_tiles emits every 120 px stride window with no density gate at all, so the render class is a filtered subset (30 percent package or more by the shader's own mask) and the photo class is unfiltered. Leak 5 was closed at the level of FILES, via the SHELF_FACE subject list, and is still open at the level of CROPS: on/tile_03, on/tile_04, on/tile_07 and off/tile_12 are ceiling, department signage and glass floral cooler, content no render crop can ever hold. NOT load-bearing for my 100 percent - I called every tile on rendering evidence and 4 of the 18 renders (on/00, on/12, off/17, off/18) do show floor and a corridor, so a critic riding is-there-a-floor takes 4 misses - but the photo class is not testing what the harness claims. FIX: gate photo crops on a photo-side density proxy, or lower MIN_PROD to a value a chase plate can reach (0.19 or less) and let the CHASE guard do its job.

The price rail has no cross-section and the tags are decals on it - one flat plane to a hard black boundary, no returns, no channel, no shadow line, and a tag hangs 4 px below its own holder while its neighbour starts 5 px higher with nothing registering to a datum.

The aisle floor. It carries luminance that nothing in the scene causes, and none that everything in the scene should cause. Frames r27_on_chase_a4, chase_a1, chase_a6, region the centre-bottom third, floor x 360-960 y 330-690. (a) a large amorphous bright pool with dark curling filaments sits mid-aisle; the ceiling troffers are long thin rectangles running across the aisle and their specular images on a real floor are long thin streaks converging to the vanishing point, whereas these filaments curl, cross the tile seams without regard to perspective, and subtend the same size at 4 m and at 12 m. (b) nothing standing on the floor darkens it - shoes, all four cart casters, the endcap barrel base and every gondola kick plate meet the floor with zero contact darkening, while in the matched Ingles reference at the same apparent distance every caster has one. OBSERVATION confidence HIGH, verified at 10x on three poses in BOTH arms and against two reference photographs. EXPLANATION confidence MEDIUM and stated separately: one term explains both, a floor lit by something with no occlusion - a baked lightmap or a constant ambient - with the swirl part of that baked albedo rather than a live reflection. Alternatives I could not rule out: shadows exist but the floor is not a shadow RECEIVER; the shadow cascade does not reach 12 m; or the swirl is a deliberate polished-floor decal and is a SEPARATE cue. FALSIFIERS - and do NOT test this with an image-row statistic, the floor is a receding surface and that is retired. F1 translate ONE object 1 m and diff the floor pixels under and around it; if any floor pixel changes the floor IS a shadow receiver and (b) is wrong. F2 render the pose from two cameras 0.5 m apart; if the filaments slide relative to the tile seams they are a live reflection and my explanation is wrong even though (a) stands. F3 contact darkening at 1.5 m but not 12 m would make this a shadow-RANGE bug rather than an absent light - PARTIALLY RUN, a tilted price card at 1.5 m in near_a4 casts nothing onto the card behind it, which favours no occlusion term at all, but a card is near-coplanar so this is not conclusive.

The aisle floor carries luminance nothing in the scene causes and none that everything in the scene should - curling filaments that ignore tile-seam perspective and subtend the same size at 4 m and 12 m, and NOTHING standing on the floor darkens it: not shoes, not any of four cart casters, not the endcap base, not one kick plate, while every caster in the matched Ingles reference has a contact shadow.

store.note: THE MATCHED-ARM FORCED CHOICE IS RETIRED AND THE CRITIC PROVED IT RATHER THAN FAILING IT. Position tally 18 second against 2 first over 20 trials, all six high-confidence calls were second and only 2 of 6 correct, and the control nobody had thought to add - CATCH TRIALS - came back 2 of 8: on 6 OF 8 PAIRS WHOSE TWO HALVES WERE THE SAME IMAGE it invented a specific named geometric difference, three at high or medium confidence. Randomising position per trial is not enough because the pairwise question itself is answerable by position. Four rounds of this project's headline perceptual number came from an instrument that will confabulate a detailed difference between two copies of one image. Any instrument that asks a scorer to find a difference must include trials with no difference in them. THEN IT PRODUCED THE FIRST POSITIVE RESULT IN 28 ROUNDS: absolute single-image classification, one crop one arm judged against a criterion fixed in advance, 10 of 12 at p 0.019 with 5 of 5 at high confidence, near_a1 4/4, near_a7 4/4, near_a4 2/4, and no chase percept at any pose. That is the first evidence here that a change is visible to a scorer who did not build it, and it independently confirms round 27's near/chase split. That instrument is now the standard. LEAK 9: the two arms differed in tag CONTENT and card SIZE, not only the geometry under test - the same slot renders 3.99 in one arm and 3.08 in the other with one card 50% taller - so the pair was solvable by reading a price. A dial that also re-rolls content is not a dial. AND WHOLE FRAMES CHANGED WHAT GETS CALLED ON: not one render was named from a shelf-edge detail, and the rail that round 27 rebuilt was never the tell in any frame, even though the single-image test shows it IS visible when you ask about it. Both are true - render-recall asks what a viewer volunteers, and the bar is written in that question.

THE MONITOR WALL NEVER BLOWS A FLUORESCENT, AND ON THREE CHANNELS IT MATHEMATICALLY CANNOT. Six of eight wall channels contain ZERO pixels above luma 0.98; five never reach 0.98 anywhere. Driving the feed to full saturation (gain 6.0, one page load) and reading the value each panel plateaus at - max equals p99.9 exactly, a perfect flat ceiling - gives CH04 0.9468, CH05 0.9580, CH08 0.9479, i.e. algebraically incapable. The source is src/cctv/shaders.js:550 in ScreenShader: col = col * 0.960 + 0.017, whose maximum is 0.977, composed with col *= uPanel at :556 (implied uPanel 0.969-1.018, so non-active panels land at 0.947-0.972). Only the active-panel 1.0 + uActive*0.13 and the glass sheen can push one back over, which is why CH01 clips and the rest do not. THIS IS ROUND 9'S OWN HEADLINE BUG ONE PASS DOWNSTREAM - 'the asymptote was exactly 1.0, so nothing could clip, for any input, by algebra.' The comment above the line is correct physics (an LCD's black leak means a screen showing black is never truly black) but the affine raises the floor AND lowers the white point; a leak should do only the first. That it matters visually and not merely numerically: reduce every reference photo to the wall's own 142x80 tile and 14 OF 14 STILL CONTAIN BLOWN PIXELS (median 0.224%, 12 of 14 still hit exactly 1.0), while the game's tiles are grey-brown mush with no lamp at all. SECOND MECHANISM, also live: even on panels that CAN clip, shipped play gives 0.00% - the wall renders raw at 2x tile size and the grade quad bilinearly averages a 2.05x tube against dark ceiling IN LINEAR, BEFORE THE SHOULDER. That is downscale-then-clip, where a real DVR substream is clip-then-downscale.

The threshold 1.27 is validated at ONE camera distance. Selectivity (pct of class clearing the selector, lamp:card) is 40x at the published z=-11.6 poses but collapses to 1.9x at z=-15 and INVERTS to 0.82x at z=-16 in the same aisle (BLADE 2.926 pct vs LENS 2.395 pct). BLADE p99 goes 1.1262 (z=-11.6) to 1.3135 (z=-16), above the threshold, while LENS p90 falls 1.4670 to 1.0640, below it. The shipped bloomSeparation() check reports both margins negative there. audio.note: It DISPROVED my hypothesis before trusting it: muting the whole pa bus left the hiss intact and the speech bus reads exact digital silence when closed, so the round-3 open-channel hiss was properly gated all along. PA had two causes in audio: echoCancellation on speakers (Chrome's AEC references the page's own render stream, which contains the player's voice returning from the ceiling 10-200ms later - it was subtracting the thing it was protecting), and the voice arriving at parity with the bed so opening the channel made the mix 4.3 dBA QUIETER because the two ducks outweighed the voice they made room for. THIRD BUG found while validating: the howl watchdog had never fired and COULD not - it read the output of a 6:1 compressor thresholded at -26dBFS against 0.30 linear, which needs +85dBFS at its input. Rebuilt on the raw mic with a steadiness discriminator, because level alone cannot separate a shout from a howl.
audio.verdict: PASS on both bugs. HISS: airTop in bed.js used filt('highshelf', 5200, 0.7, 6) on pink noise - pink falls 3dB/octave, so a +6dB shelf spanning two octaves flattens it EXACTLY, generating WHITE noise above 5kHz, which is the definition of tape hiss. 11.2kHz band went -46.6 -> -69.8dB while everything below 5.6kHz moved under 2dB.

The aisle floor. It carries luminance that nothing in the scene causes, and none that everything in the scene should cause. Frames r27_on_chase_a4, chase_a1, chase_a6, region the centre-bottom third, floor x 360-960 y 330-690. (a) a large amorphous bright pool with dark curling filaments sits mid-aisle; the ceiling troffers are long thin rectangles running across the aisle and their specular images on a real floor are long thin streaks converging to the vanishing point, whereas these filaments curl, cross the tile seams without regard to perspective, and subtend the same size at 4 m and at 12 m. (b) nothing standing on the floor darkens it - shoes, all four cart casters, the endcap barrel base and every gondola kick plate meet the floor with zero contact darkening, while in the matched Ingles reference at the same apparent distance every caster has one. OBSERVATION confidence HIGH, verified at 10x on three poses in BOTH arms and against two reference photographs. EXPLANATION confidence MEDIUM and stated separately: one term explains both, a floor lit by something with no occlusion - a baked lightmap or a constant ambient - with the swirl part of that baked albedo rather than a live reflection. Alternatives I could not rule out: shadows exist but the floor is not a shadow RECEIVER; the shadow cascade does not reach 12 m; or the swirl is a deliberate polished-floor decal and is a SEPARATE cue. FALSIFIERS - and do NOT test this with an image-row statistic, the floor is a receding surface and that is retired. F1 translate ONE object 1 m and diff the floor pixels under and around it; if any floor pixel changes the floor IS a shadow receiver and (b) is wrong. F2 render the pose from two cameras 0.5 m apart; if the filaments slide relative to the tile seams they are a live reflection and my explanation is wrong even though (a) stands. F3 contact darkening at 1.5 m but not 12 m would make this a shadow-RANGE bug rather than an absent light - PARTIALLY RUN, a tilted price card at 1.5 m in near_a4 casts nothing onto the card behind it, which favours no occlusion term at all, but a card is near-coplanar so this is not conclusive.
